title: Descent completion of a prestack using covering sieves
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-topos] whose objects and arrows form sets in the larger universe; all groupoids and their morphism sets below belong to that universe. A fibred groupoid has cartesian pullbacks along every base arrow, with their coherent comparison isomorphisms. A prestack is a fibred groupoid whose presheaves of isomorphisms on slice sites are sheaves. A stack is a prestack in which covering descent data for objects are effective. Let $\mathcal Q$ be a prestack. For a covering sieve $R\in J(T)$, regard $R$ as a full subcategory of $\mathcal C/T$. Write $\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(R)$ for its groupoid of cartesian sections: a section assigns $x_f\in\mathcal Q(V)$ to each $f:V\to T$ in $R$ and coherent isomorphisms $h^*x_f\cong x_{fh}$ for each $h:W\to V$; its arrows are compatible families of fibre isomorphisms. Define $\mathcal D\mathcal Q(T)$ to have objects $(R,x)$ with $R\in J(T)$ and $x\in\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(R)$, and arrows
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D\mathcal Q(T)}((R,x),(S,y))=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq R\cap S,\ K\in J(T)}\operatorname{Isom}_{\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(K)}(x|_K,y|_K),$$
where the transition maps restrict to smaller covering sieves. Composition is composition on a common covering subsieve; pullback along $h:V\to T$ restricts a section along $\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal C/T$, to the inverse-image sieve $h^*R$. These formulas give a fibred groupoid $\mathcal D\mathcal Q$ which is a stack. Sending $u\in\mathcal Q(T)$ to its pullback section on the maximal sieve defines a pullback-compatible functor $e:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal D\mathcal Q$ fully faithful on every fibre. If $(R,x)\in\mathcal D\mathcal Q(T)$ and $f:V\to T$ is in $R$, then $(R,x)|_V$ is canonically isomorphic to $e(x_f)$, compatibly with restriction and the section's transition isomorphisms. In particular these formulas include empty covering sieves whenever they belong to $J$.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction in both proofs, including checks (1)-(8) in the naive proof; covering-sieve formulation avoids requiring fibre products of arbitrary base arrows.

proof.text: Use the topology axioms in [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Covering sieves are upward closed: if $R\subseteq S$ covers, then $f^*S$ is maximal for $f\in R$, so transitivity makes $S$ cover. If $R,S$ cover, then for $f\in R$ the sieve $f^*(R\cap S)=f^*S$ covers, so $R\cap S$ covers. If $R$ covers and each $S_f$ covers $\operatorname{dom}f$, the sieve $H=\{fg:f\in R,\ g\in S_f\}$ covers: it is a sieve, and $f^*H\supseteq S_f$, so use upward closure and transitivity. Thus common covering refinements exist. All sieve sets, section data, families of isomorphisms and their quotients are sets in the fixed larger universe, being subsets, indexed products and quotients of sets there.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text:
For two objects $(R,x),(S,y)$, apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-section-covering-restriction] with $S$ there equal to $R\cap S$ here and any covering $K\subseteq R\cap S$. Its hypothesis holds since pullback of a covering sieve is covering. Hence every restriction
$\operatorname{Isom}(x|_{R\cap S},y|_{R\cap S})\to\operatorname{Isom}(x|_K,y|_K)$
is bijective. The stated colimit is the quotient of pairs $(K,\alpha)$ by equality after a common refinement; every pair has a unique extension to $R\cap S$. This identifies the colimit canonically with the first isomorphism set. In particular a section isomorphism on any covering common subsieve represents an arrow uniquely, and equality can be checked on any further covering subsieve.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text: Compose representatives after restricting to the intersection of their sieves. Changing a representative does not change the composite, since on the intersection of the witnessing refinements the component composites agree. Identities are the identity section families and inverses are the component inverses. The category axioms hold after restriction to one common covering sieve, where they are those of $\mathcal Q$. Pullback of a representative on $K$ along $h$ is its component family on $h^*K$; it respects the quotient because inverse image preserves intersections and coverings. The unit and composite-pullback comparisons are those of the cartesian section components of $\mathcal Q$; their coherence holds componentwise. These fibre groupoids and coherent pullbacks give the total fibred groupoid explicitly: an arrow over $h:V\to T$ from $A$ to $B$ is an arrow $A\to h^*B$ in the fibre at $V$, and composition uses the just specified pullback comparisons. The arrows $h^*B\to B$ represented by identities are cartesian by this description of all arrows over composites.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text: Define $e(u)$ by $f\mapsto f^*u$ on the maximal sieve. Its section comparisons and its compatibility with pullback are the given cartesian comparisons of $\mathcal Q$. By step 2 a morphism $e(u)\to e(v)$ is uniquely a section isomorphism on the maximal sieve. Evaluation at $1_T$ identifies these with $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Q(T)}(u,v)$: naturality forces the component at $f$ to be the pullback of the component at $1_T$. Thus $e$ is fully faithful. If $f\in R$, then $f^*R$ is maximal, and the comparisons $h^*x_f\cong x_{fh}$ give a section isomorphism $e(x_f)\cong(R,x)|_V$. Coherence of $x$ makes these isomorphisms compatible with restriction and its transition maps.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text: Prove descent of arrows in $\mathcal D\mathcal Q$. Let $A=(S,x),B=(U,y)$ lie over $T$, and let a compatible family $\alpha_f:A|_V\to B|_V$ be given on a covering sieve $R$. Put $H=R\cap S\cap U$. For $f\in H$, the local isomorphisms of step 4 identify $A|_V,B|_V$ with $e(x_f),e(y_f)$. Full faithfulness of $e$ gives a unique $a_f:x_f\to y_f$ representing $\alpha_f$. Naturality of the $\alpha_f$ and faithfulness of $e$ make $(a_f)$ a section isomorphism on $H$, hence an arrow $a:A\to B$. For arbitrary $f\in R$, its restriction agrees with $\alpha_f$ on the covering sieve $f^*H$; step 2, now over $V$, proves equality. Any other glued arrow agrees on $H$ and is equal by step 2. This argument works over every slice object, so all isomorphism presheaves of $\mathcal D\mathcal Q$ are sheaves: it is a prestack.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text:
Now let $A$ be cartesian object descent data in $\mathcal D\mathcal Q$ on a covering sieve $R$ of $T$. For each $f:V\to T$ in $R$, choose its displayed representative $A_f=(S_f,x^f)$. Form the covering sieve $H=\{fg:f\in R,\ g\in S_f\}$ from step 1. For each $t\in H$ choose one factorization $t=f_tg_t$, and put $z_t=x^{f_t}_{g_t}$. Step 4 followed by the transition of $A$ gives an isomorphism $b_t:e(z_t)\to A_t$. For $h:W\to\operatorname{dom}t$ with $s=th$, form
$$e(h^*z_t)\cong h^*e(z_t)\xrightarrow{h^*b_t}h^*A_t\xrightarrow{c_{t,h}}A_s\xrightarrow{b_s^{-1}}e(z_s).$$
Full faithfulness of $e$ lifts this uniquely to $d_{t,h}:h^*z_t\to z_s$. The identities and cocycle for $d$ follow by applying the faithful $e$: the intermediate $b$ and $b^{-1}$ cancel and the remaining equality is exactly the cocycle for $c$, with the cartesian comparison isomorphisms inserted. Hence $z$ is a cartesian $\mathcal Q$-section on $H$, and $B=(H,z)$ is an actual object of the prescribed completion. No effectiveness in $\mathcal Q$ was assumed: only arrow lifting along the already proved fully faithful $e$ was used.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text: For each $t\in H$, step 4 gives $l_t:e(z_t)\to B|_{\operatorname{dom}t}$. The arrows $b_t l_t^{-1}:B|_{\operatorname{dom}t}\to A_t$ are compatible: the required equation is precisely $c_{t,h}h^*b_t=b_{th}e(d_{t,h})$, which defined $d_{t,h}$ in step 6, and $l$ has the same transition equation. Apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-section-covering-restriction] to the prestack $\mathcal D\mathcal Q$ proved in step 5, the inclusion $H\subseteq R$, and its two sections $B|_R,A$. For every $f\in R$, the sieve $f^*H$ covers by stability of coverings, so all the lemma's hypotheses hold. It extends this compatible isomorphism uniquely from $H$ to $R$. Thus $B$ with this isomorphism realizes the given descent data. Together with step 5 this is exactly the stack condition.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), final descent-data construction, naive checks (1)-(8) and less naive construction; explicit covering-sieve verification.

proof.text: If $\varnothing\in J(T)$, its unique cartesian section gives the object $(\varnothing,*)$. For any two objects of the completion the empty common refinement contributes a unique section isomorphism, and step 2 shows this is their unique arrow. Thus the fibre is nonempty and contractible; descent on an empty covering has exactly the required effectiveness and uniqueness. Pullback stability gives the same assertion on every inverse-image empty covering. None of the preceding constructions chose an element of an empty sieve: in step 6 the choices are only indexed by actual members of $H$. Hence the empty cases are included without an added nonemptiness assumption.
